mainEntity.name: Can you design on top of our existing brand?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The design system starts from your current colours and fonts, and we only change what fails readability or accessibility, with the reason written down.
کنتراست رنگ، مسیر صفحه‌کلید، حالت فوکوس و برچسب فرم‌ها را بر اساس WCAG 2.2 سطح AA بررسی و نتیجه را در مشخصات تحویل ثبت می‌کنیم.
We check colour contrast, keyboard path, focus states and form labels against WCAG 2.2 level AA, and record the result in the handover spec.

UI/UX design
Interfaces decided by user tasks and evidence, delivered as a system developers can actually build from.
Problem

items: A design that looks good in the design file but says nothing about error, empty or mobile states changes during build. Developers guess, users cannot find the button, and every new screen is designed from scratch.

blocks.html: Who it is for

items: Teams with a product or web app whose users get stuck on a specific task (sign-up, checkout, reporting).
Startups that want to test core flows with real users before building.
Development teams that need a buildable design system, not a set of separate pictures.

blocks.html: Who it is not for

items: If you only need a few screens to show investors.
If you want design done with no access to users or data and the result declared "final". We can work without evidence, but the output states which decision rests on which assumption.
If you need native iOS or Android app design to platform guidelines.

blocks.html: Approach

items: Tasks. Input: a conversation with you and any existing data (support tickets, analytics). Output: the main user tasks, ranked. Owner: dadmor with you.
Flows. Input: the task list. Output: flow map and wireframes of key flows. Owner: dadmor; approval: you.
System. Input: approved wireframes. Output: design system (tokens and components with every state) and key screens. Owner: dadmor.
Test. Input: a clickable prototype. Output: user test notes and a list of fixes. Owner: dadmor; recruiting test users: you.
Handover. Input: the revised design. Output: a developer handover spec. Owner: dadmor.

blocks.html: Deliverables
Scope and timeline factors

items: What moves the work from S to M to L: number of flows and key screens, number of user roles, bilingual layouts, and whether user testing is in scope.
What you supply: access to the current product, any user data you have, and test users.
What delays projects: test users who cannot be found, and feature priorities that change mid-design.

blocks.html: Effort band

items: Band S, M or L by number of flows and key screens. We give a fixed price after the scoping conversation, in a written proposal.

blocks.html: A band is the rough size of the work, not a price and not a duration. A fixed price is set only after a scoping conversation, in a written proposal.
The band is a starting estimate; the scoping conversation may move it.
Limits and risks

items: Testing with a few users reveals major problems, but the result is not statistical and we do not present it that way.
Building the design is not part of this service; if you want it built, we scope Website building alongside it.
If you cannot provide test users, we test with people similar to your audience and say so in the test notes.
